headline: Dry high pressure keeps both regions sunny; the Upstate warms faster this weekend
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Clear, cool northeast flow continues today, followed by a dry and mostly sunny weekend. Afternoon temperatures hold in the middle 70s, while sheltered Bluegrass locations can fall into the middle 40s at night.

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: No hazardous weather expected; brief early river-valley fog has dissipated
days.forecast: Sunny and dry after a cool start. Northeast wind 4–8 mph, with a few afternoon gusts possible near Lexington. Thin high clouds may arrive tonight, but the eastern Bluegrass should stay mostly clear and cool quickly after sunset.

days.label: Saturday
days.forecast: Mostly sunny, dry and pleasantly cool. Light northeast wind and low humidity continue. Clearer eastern and sheltered locations have the best chance to reach the lower or middle 40s Saturday night.

days.label: Sunday
days.forecast: Sunny with only a few passing high clouds. Light north to northeast wind. Temperatures change little from Saturday, and no organized precipitation is expected through Monday morning.

kentucky.bottomLine: The high-confidence signal is three dry days with highs in the 70s. The only meaningful uncertainty is how cold sheltered Bluegrass valleys become Saturday night.

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson / Central primary · Tempest excluded
upstate.summary: Morning low clouds around Clemson and Central scatter out today. Dry high pressure then brings sunny conditions and a steady warming trend, from the upper 70s today to the middle 80s Sunday.

currentConditions.condition: Direct machine-readable retrieval was unavailable; official KCEU and KLQK observations used instead

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: No hazardous weather expected; morning low clouds should clear by late morning
days.forecast: Morning clouds scatter out, leaving a sunny and dry afternoon. Light northeast wind around 3–7 mph. Clear skies and light wind tonight allow temperatures to fall into the lower 50s.

days.label: Saturday
days.forecast: Sunny and warmer as the shallow cool wedge fully erodes. Wind becomes light and variable, generally under 5 mph. Low humidity and clear skies continue Saturday night.

days.label: Sunday
days.forecast: Sunny and warmer, with light west to southwest wind during the afternoon. Dry air prevents meaningful convection, and no rain is expected through Monday morning.

upstate.bottomLine: Low clouds are the only short-term complication. Once they break today, the forecast is high confidence: dry weather, cool nights and progressively warmer afternoons through Sunday.
upstate.confidence: High overall; moderate on the exact clearing time and Saturday high-temperature range

sourceNotes: NWS point forecasts were generated at 9:13 AM EDT. Official airport observations span 8:35–9:05 AM EDT, and Kentucky Mesonet DANV reported at 9:15 AM EDT.
The Louisville and Greenville-Spartanburg Area Forecast Discussions were issued at 6:51 AM and 6:50 AM EDT, respectively. Both support dry weather through the forecast period.
The NWS active-alert API returned no active alerts for either the Danville or Clemson forecast point at the 9:13 AM EDT check. This official-alert status is separate from the independent analysis.

NOMADS inventories checked at 9:13 AM EDT showed HRRR through 12Z, RAP through 11Z, NAM through 12Z, and complete 06Z GFS and GEFS cycles. NEXLAB showed complete 06Z NAM, NAM Nest, GFS and GEFS cycles and a complete 00Z ECMWF cycle.

College of DuPage NEXLAB panels were checked directly. The 12Z HRRR and 06Z NAM/NAM Nest/GFS/GEFS plus 00Z ECMWF panels consistently support dry conditions; the 1:11 PM UTC visible satellite showed residual patchy low cloud, and the concurrent Southeast radar mosaic showed no organized echoes over either region.
Direct machine-readable Clemson Weather Network retrieval was unavailable, so KCEU and KLQK official observations were used. Tempest is excluded from Upstate analysis and verification.
Radar and satellite links remain external and live; the existing Google Sites radar section is not modified by this candidate.
